feedback.problem: What is the limit of the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{3{n}^{4}-{n}^{2}}{5-2{n}^{4}}$ for $n\ge 1?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To determine whether the sequence converges or diverges, we need to determine the limit of the sequence as $n$ approaches infinity:

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n}=\frac{3{n}^{4}-{n}^{2}}{5-2{n}^{4}}.
$$

The dominant term in the denominator is $-2{n}^{4},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{4}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{3{n}^{4}-{n}^{2}}{5-2{n}^{4}} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{3{n}^{4}}{{n}^{4}}-\frac{{n}^{2}}{{n}^{4}})}{(\frac{5}{{n}^{4}}-\frac{2{n}^{4}}{{n}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(3-\frac{1}{{n}^{2}})}{\frac{5}{{n}^{4}}-2} \\  & =\frac{3-0}{0-2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the limit exists, the sequence converges, and its limit is $-\frac{3}{2}.$
